items.subject: MA
items.prompt: How many kilograms are in 65,000 grams?
items.explanation: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 kg = 1,000 g. Going from grams (small) to kilograms (big), the number gets smaller: 65,000 ÷ 1,000 = 65 kg.
items.misconceptions: divides by the wrong power of ten

why.A: 6.5 kg divides by 10,000. A kilogram is 1,000 grams, so divide by 1,000.
why.C: 650 kg takes away only two zeros. 1,000 grams make 1 kilogram, so divide by 1,000.
why.D: 6,500 kg takes away only one zero. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so divide by 1,000.

items.prompt: How many grams are in 3 kilograms?
items.explanation: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Going from a big unit to a small one, the number gets bigger: 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 g.
items.misconceptions: multiplies by the wrong power of ten

why.A: 3 g keeps the same number. A kilogram is much heavier than a gram, so there are many more grams.

items.subject: MA
items.subskill: adding a mass in grams to one in kilograms
items.prompt: One box weighs 4,500 grams. Another box weighs 3 kilograms. How many kilograms do the two boxes weigh together?
items.explanation: Put both in kilograms: 4,500 g ÷ 1,000 = 4.5 kg. Then 4.5 + 3 = 7.5 kg.

why.A: 4.8 kg treats 3 kilograms as 300 grams. Change 4,500 g to kilograms instead: 4.5 kg.
why.C: 48 kg adds 45 and 3. 4,500 grams is 4.5 kilograms, not 45.
why.D: 4,503 kg adds 3 to 4,500 without changing the grams into kilograms. Put both in the same unit first.

why.A: 1,502 mL adds 2 to 1,500 without changing liters to milliliters.

items.subject: MA
items.subskill: how many pieces fit, in mixed units
items.prompt: A ribbon 3 meters long is cut into pieces that are each 25 centimeters long. How many pieces are there?
items.explanation: Change meters to centimeters: 3 m = 300 cm. Then 300 ÷ 25 = 12 pieces.
items.misconceptions: divides without converting; uses the wrong conversion

why.A: 4 is the number of pieces in one meter. The ribbon is 3 meters long.
why.C: 75 multiplies 3 by 25. Fitting pieces into a length is division.
why.D: 120 uses 3,000 cm for 3 meters. 1 m = 100 cm, so 3 m = 300 cm.

items.subject: MA
items.prompt: How much is 40 ounces in pounds and ounces?
items.explanation: 1 lb = 16 oz. Two pounds is 32 oz, and 40 − 32 = 8 oz left: 2 lb 8 oz.
items.misconceptions: uses the wrong number for the unit

why.A: 4 lb uses 10 ounces in a pound. A pound is 16 ounces.
why.B: 2 lb 4 oz is only 36 ounces (32 + 4). 2 pounds is 32 ounces, and 40 − 32 = 8 left over.
why.D: 3 lb 4 oz uses 12 ounces in a pound (3 × 12 = 36, 40 − 36 = 4). A pound is 16 ounces.

items.prompt: A rectangle is 2 meters long and 50 centimeters wide. What is its perimeter in centimeters?

why.B: 250 cm adds the length and the width once. A rectangle has two of each.

items.subject: MA
items.subskill: how many batches, in mixed units
items.prompt: A muffin recipe uses 250 grams of flour. How many batches can be made from a 2-kilogram bag of flour?
items.explanation: Change the bag to grams: 2 kg = 2,000 g. Then 2,000 ÷ 250 = 8 batches.

why.B: 80 makes a zero slip in 2,000 ÷ 250. Check: 250 × 8 = 2,000.
why.C: 125 divides 250 by 2: the wrong way round, and the bag is 2,000 grams. Divide the bag by one batch: 2,000 ÷ 250.
why.D: 500 multiplies 250 by 2. Change the bag to grams and divide.
